title: Release 0.9.0: bump, build, qualify and publish the quest-only release superseding the unpublished 0.8.0 tag
description:
Ships the frozen-but-unpublished 0.8.0 content together with the 15 post-freeze commits, under the next unclaimed number. Scope ratified by opum-agent (R5); publication itself is tier 3 and goes to the repository owner directly, never on an orchestrator say-so.

WHY 0.9.0 AND NOT 0.8.0 OR 0.8.1. The v0.8.0 tag exists at 9d91fc35 and will not be re-pointed: quest-web runs a live link gate against this repository, and opum-marketplace re-resolves tag to commit to tree against a recorded baseline, so a moved tag falsifies every record citing it. The precedent for a tagged-but-unpublished version is 0.6.1 to 0.6.2 -- ship under the next unclaimed number. Relative to PUBLISHED 0.7.1 this carries a breaking change plus a feature, so the next unclaimed number is a minor one.

PAIR STATE. Not a lockstep release. lore-cli dev is 64 commits past their v0.7.0 and they intend 0.8.0, but they are gated on LCLI-533 and on qualification ordering. OPAG-142 already qualified lore 0.7.0 with quest 0.7.1 as a non-lockstep pair, so the pair does not mean equal strings. The CHANGELOG declares the break, as the convention requires.

KNOWN HAZARD IN THIS SEQUENCE. Building rewrites npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest, and on this host an executed freshly-built darwin-arm64 binary makes any git read of that path SIGKILL (exit 137, QCLI-271). The runbook ordering is mandatory: do every execution first, then delete and recreate the file from an untouched copy of the build artifact as the literal last step before git touches it, with zero execution in between.

ALSO IN FLIGHT, NOT BLOCKING. opum-cli-e2e needs two artifacts from the qualification run to bind their pair qualification: the candidate bundle and the native-execution receipt. They need the run id and the tag, and have asked for a SHA quoted as v0.9.0^{commit} rather than git rev-parse v0.9.0, which returns the tag object for an annotated tag.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every hand-edited version site named in the release runbook carries 0.9.0, verified by re-reading each file rather than by trusting the runbook list -- package.json version and its six optionalDependencies pins, src/application/version.ts, src/contract/tracker/index.ts, fixtures/tracker/v1/conformance.json, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
bun.lock platform pins are regenerated rather than left at the previous version, since nothing automates this and a stale lockfile breaks the frozen-lockfile install in CI.
All six platform packages are rebuilt and their checksum map matches, with bun run check and bun run test:packages both exiting 0.
CHANGELOG Unreleased is renamed to 0.9.0 at tag time AND a fresh empty Unreleased heading is left above it -- the omission of the successor is what produced QCLI-319.
dev is promoted to main by fast-forward after the required contexts go green on that exact SHA, and the promoted ref is asserted by reading it back from the API rather than from the push exit code.
The v0.9.0 tag is created and the v0.8.0 tag is left pointing at 9d91fc35.

Publication is performed only under explicit authorization from the repository owner, obtained immediately before it, and the registry state is re-checked afterward rather than inferred from the publish exit code.

implementationNotes:
PROGRESS as of the byte commit, branch chore/QCLI-347-release-0.9.0, two commits landed on the branch and not yet merged.

STRINGS (5347d5d). All six hand-edited sites moved to 0.9.0 and each re-read after the edit rather than trusted from the runbook list: package.json .version plus its six optionalDependencies pins, src/application/version.ts QUEST_VERSION, src/contract/tracker/index.ts QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION, fixtures/tracker/v1/conformance.json questVersion, .claude-plugin/plugin.json .version. A grep for 0.8.0 across src, fixtures, .claude-plugin and package.json returns nothing afterward, so this bump had no undiscovered sixth site -- the runbook list was accurate for this release, which is worth recording because it has drifted before. bun.lock regenerated under bun 1.3.14 (matching packageManager) so its platform pins move with the bump and configVersion survives.

BYTES (4b60e7a). All six platforms rebuilt, including bun-windows-aarch64 which needs 1.3.x. CLAUDE.md managed block regenerated to 0.9.0 by running agents --update-instructions against the FRESHLY BUILT darwin-arm64 binary, not the global install: it reported version-only before and current after.

QCLI-271 SIGKILL: handled by the runbook ordering, and the hazard was OBSERVED rather than merely avoided. Pristine copy of the darwin-arm64 binary taken before any execution; all executions done (--version reporting 0.9.0, agents --check, agents --update-instructions); git status then exited 137 exactly as predicted; delete-and-recreate from the pristine copy cleared it (old inode 37849830, new 37850022, sha256 identical at 0dbf171e...). So it is a new inode, not new bytes.

GREEN ON THE BRANCH: bun run check exit 0 at 592 pass / 0 fail; check:packages exit 0; test:packages exit 0. git status clean after those executions, which confirms the CLAUDE.md re-measurement that a CLEAN index does not re-arm the kill.

REMAINING: open the PR, merge to dev, promote dev to main by fast-forward, rename CHANGELOG Unreleased to 0.9.0 AND leave a fresh empty Unreleased above it (QCLI-319), tag v0.9.0, dispatch the qualification workflow against the tag, then seek the owner authorization that publication requires. Nothing is published and nothing is tagged yet.

PUBLISHED. @opum-ai/quest 0.9.0 and all six platform packages are live. Verified end to end against the registry and against a real consumer install, not from the publisher exit code.

  npm view @opum-ai/quest version        0.9.0
  packument dist-tags.latest             0.9.0
  0.9.0 published at                     2026-09-19T00:37:46.553Z
  npm install @opum-ai/quest@0.9.0       17 packages, binary reports 0.9.0,
                                         quest-darwin-arm64 resolved, and
                                         task create --id <taken> returns
                                         validation -- QCLI-346 live in the
                                         published bytes.

ROUTE: the Keychain granular token (npm-opum-ai-publish), after the owner ran security unlock-keychain. No OTP was needed or accepted on that route. No attestations, as expected for the token path, matching 0.6.2/0.7.0/0.7.1.

TWO THINGS THAT LOOKED LIKE FAILURES AND WERE PROPAGATION LAG. Both are worth recording because both produced a confident wrong reading at the time.

1. quest-linux-arm64 did not appear within the publisher visibility window (33 checks). It was absent from versions AND from time, with time.modified unchanged since the 0.7.1 release -- which is the exact signature the runbook records for the 0.7.0 STAGED incident. The publisher correctly refused to publish the wrapper and reported absent-or-staged, and npm stage list could not adjudicate because it returned E401 for the publishing token. Re-running with --diagnose-staged, under separate owner authorization, resolved it immediately: skip, already on the registry at this version. So it had landed all along and was simply slow. Staged, never-landed and SLOW are three states, and the first read cannot separate them.

2. The wrapper then did the same thing. The publisher reported published and verified with a genuine exit 0, while two independent anonymous reads disagreed -- cache-busted packument had no 0.9.0, and the targeted version endpoint returned HTTP 404. It appeared about 60 seconds later, and the packument lagged the version endpoint by a further interval, so two npm cache layers disagreed with each other while both were being read honestly.

A TOOLING FINDING FROM OUR OWN PUBLISHER, filed separately. The line "@opum-ai/quest <version> published and verified (N check(s))" names the wrapper, but waitForPublished(receipt, version) verifies the SIX PLATFORM PACKAGES against the receipt digests. It does not assert the wrapper is readable. The write returning success and the platforms matching the receipt are two different facts about two different objects, and the sentence attributes both to the wrapper.

A SECOND TOOLING FINDING, also filed separately: a credential that is present but unreadable and one that is absent have opposite remedies, and resolveToken collapses both into no stored token found.
finalSummary:
quest 0.9.0 is published and live on npm: wrapper plus all six platform packages, verified by a real consumer install rather than by the publisher exit code.

WHAT SHIPPED AND WHY THE NUMBER MOVED. 0.8.0 was frozen, tagged at 9d91fc35 and never published; fifteen commits then landed on dev, five of them consumer-observable, with an empty Unreleased heading above the frozen section. The tag was not re-pointed -- quest-web runs a live link gate against this repository and opum-marketplace re-resolves tag to commit to tree against a recorded baseline -- so the content shipped under the next unclaimed number, per the 0.6.1-to-0.6.2 precedent. Relative to published 0.7.1 this is breaking plus feature, so the next unclaimed number was a minor one.

VERIFIED: npm view @opum-ai/quest version returns 0.9.0; dist-tags.latest is 0.9.0; npm install @opum-ai/quest@0.9.0 adds 17 packages, resolves quest-darwin-arm64, runs and reports 0.9.0, and returns the new QCLI-346 validation error for a taken --id, proving the fix is in the published bytes. main is at e8eeaf1, v0.9.0 peels to it, and v0.8.0 remains at 9d91fc35.

THE PART WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. Two packages appeared to fail and had merely not propagated. quest-linux-arm64 missed the publisher visibility window entirely, presenting the exact signature the runbook records for the 0.7.0 staged incident -- absent from versions, absent from time, time.modified unchanged -- and npm stage list returned E401 for the publishing token, so nothing available to the publisher could adjudicate it. --diagnose-staged, run under separate owner authorization, found it already on the registry. The wrapper then repeated the pattern, with two npm cache layers disagreeing with each other. STAGED, NEVER-LANDED and SLOW are three states and a single read separates none of them; the runbook currently names only the first two.

The publish gate itself worked exactly as designed and is the reason none of this reached a consumer: with a platform package unresolvable, the wrapper was not published, so nothing ever advertised an optionalDependency that could not resolve. That is the 0.7.0 failure mode being prevented rather than repeated.

TWO DEFECTS IN OUR OWN RELEASE TOOLING were found while doing this and are filed rather than fixed here: the published-and-verified message names the wrapper while verifying the platform packages, and resolveToken reports a present-but-unreadable credential as an absent one. Both are the same shape as QCLI-346 -- two cases with different remedies collapsed into one message.

PROCESS NOTE, recorded because it cost real work: tracker edits made on dev and left uncommitted were destroyed by a git reset --hard origin/dev during branch setup. Six checked criteria and a long progress note had to be reconstructed. Tracker writes are working-tree changes; make them on a branch and commit them promptly.
